title: International Consensus classification (ICC) Diagnostic critères pour primaire Myelofibrosis (PMF)
abbreviations: International Consensus Classification (ICC) Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Myelofibrosis (PMF)
formula:
The diagnosis of primary myelofibrosis (PMF) is defined by the presence of all three major criteria and at least one minor criterion confirmed in two consecutive determinations:

| PMF, Early/prefibrotic Stage (Pre-PMF) | PMF, Overt Fibrotic Stage |
| --- | --- |
| Major Criteria: 1. Bone marrow biopsy showing megakaryocytic proliferation and atypia 1 , bone marrow fibrosis grade <2, increased age-adjusted BM cellularity, granulocytic proliferation, and (often) decreased erythropoiesis 2. JAK2 , CALR , or MPL mutation 2 or presence of another clonal marker 3 or absence of reactive bone marrow reticulin fibrosis 4 3. Diagnostic criteria for BCR::ABL1 -positive CML, PV, ET, myelodysplastic syndromes, or other myeloid neoplasms are not met Minor Criteria: Anemia not attributed to a comorbid condition Leukocytosis ≥11 × 10 9 /L Palpable splenomegaly Lactate dehydrogenase level above the reference range | Major Criteria: 1. Bone marrow biopsy showing megakaryocytic proliferation and atypia 1 , accompanied by reticulin and/or collagen fibrosis grades 2 or 3 2. JAK2 , CALR , or MPL mutation 2 or presence of another clonal marker 3 or absence of reactive myelofibrosis 4 3. Diagnostic criteria for ET, PV, BCR::ABL1 -positive CML, myelodysplastic syndrome, or other myeloid neoplasms 5 are not met Minor Criteria: Anemia not attributed to a comorbid condition Leukocytosis ≥11 × 10 9 /L Palpable splenomegaly Lactate dehydrogenase level above the above the reference range Leukoerythroblastosis |

1. Morphology of megakaryocytes in pre-PMF and overt PMF usually demonstrates a higher degree of megakaryocytic atypia than in any other MPN subtype; distinctive features of megakaryocytes include small to giant megakaryocytes with a prevalence of severe maturation defects (cloud-like, hypolobulated, and hyperchromatic nuclei) and presence of abnormal large dense clusters (mostly >6 megakaryocytes lying strictly adjacent).
2. It is recommended to use highly sensitive assays for *JAK2* V617F (sensitivity level <1%) and *CALR* and *MPL* (sensitivity level 1% to 3%); in negative cases, consider searching for noncanonical *JAK2* and *MPL* mutations.
3. Assessed by cytogenetics or sensitive NGS techniques; detection of mutations associated with myeloid neoplasms (eg, *ASXL1* , *EZH2* , *IDH1* , *IDH2* , *SF3B1* , *SRSF2* , and *TET2* mutations) supports the clonal nature of the disease.
4. Minimal reticulin fibrosis (grade 1) secondary to infection, autoimmune disorder or other chronic inflammatory conditions, hairy cell leukemia or another lymphoid neoplasm, metastatic malignancy, or toxic (chronic) myelopathies.
5. Monocytosis can be present at diagnosis or develop during the course of PMF; in these cases, a history of MPN excludes CMML, whereas a higher variant allelic frequency for MPN-associated driver mutations is supporting the diagnosis of PMF with monocytosis rather than CMML.

how_to_use.why:
- Fournit un cadre unifié permettant de réduire l’incertitude diagnostique et d’optimiser la prise en charge clinique.
- Il est important de distinguer la PMF préfibrotique de la PMF avérée, car elles diffèrent en termes de présentation, de progression de la maladie et de résultats de survie.
how_to_use.when: Aide au diagnostic de la myélofibrose primitive (MFP) et à distinguer la MFP manifestement fibreuse de la MFP débutante/pré-fibreuse.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Based on the 2022 International Consensus Classification (ICC) of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemias, which differs slightly from the World Health Organization (WHO) classification system.
- Prefibrotic PMF with thrombocytosis can mimic essential thrombocythemia (ET). Careful review of clinical signs and morphologic examination of megakaryocytes is necessary to distinguish between the two.

next_steps.advice:
- Utiliser les résultats de cet outil conjointement avec l'expertise clinique et les avis spécialisés pour finaliser le diagnostic et la classification de la PMF.
- Après avoir posé le diagnostic de PMF, réaliser une stratification du risque à l'aide d'un outil pronostique (p. ex., IPSS, DIPSS, MIPSS, GIPSS) afin de guider les discussions et les décisions de prise en charge.
